sections.text:
1 Foll. 28v-56v complectunctur commentarii anonymi in Ptolemaei tetrabiblum
a. 1559 Basileae impressi lib. I et II pag. 1-63 lin. 21 τόπους. Fol. 56 desinit septi-
mus quaternio, hic multa intercidisse iam vidit vir quidam doctus saec XVI qui in
marg. fol. 56v adnotavit λείπεται τέτταρα(?) φύλλα. Quae sequuntur fol. 57r usque
ad fol. 58v habentur in libro IV eiusdem commentarii a pag. 176 usque ad pagi-
nam 179 lin. 37. — Omnia contulit Boll, cui haec debemus.
2 Quae foliis 58v-75 invenies, repetuntur ff. 59-80 cod. Parisini 1991 (cf. supra,
p. 61, n. 1).
3 Nechepsonis περὶ μηνὸς opus esse dubitanter coniecit Kroll collatis Marcianis,
335, f. 340v, 336, f. 278r.
4 Cf. Riess, Nechepsonis et Petosiridis fragmenta, p. 365, no 20 sqq., qui tamen
ab hoc differt. Aliam Petosiridis Nechepsoni epistolam in cod. Mutinensi 174,
f. 262 inveniri notavit Kroll.
sections.en:
1 Fols. 28v-56v contain the anonymous commentary on Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos
printed in Basel in the year 1559, books I and II, pages 1-63, line 21 τόπους ('places'). Fol. 56 ends the sev-
enth quire, here a certain learned man of the 16th century already saw that many things had fallen out, who in the
margin of fol. 56v annotated λείπεται τέτταρα(?) φύλλα ('four(?) leaves are missing'). What follows from fol. 57r up
to fol. 58v is found in book IV of the same commentary from page 176 up to page
179, line 37. — Boll collated everything, to whom we owe these things.
2 What you will find on folios 58v-75, are repeated on ff. 59-80 of the Parisian codex 1991 (cf. above,
p. 61, n. 1).
3 Kroll hesitantly conjectured that it is the work of Nechepso περὶ μηνὸς ('on the month'), having compared the Marciani,
335, f. 340v, 336, f. 278r.
4 Cf. Riess, Nechepsonis et Petosiridis fragmenta, p. 365, no 20 sqq., which however
differs from this. Kroll noted that another letter of Petosiris to Nechepso is found in the Mutinensis codex 174,
f. 262.

summary.headline: Astrological Treatises and Monthly Lords
summary.text: Catalog entries for folios 23v–61 covering Hyphiles’ calculations, decumbitures, vomiting and purging, seasonal time transfers, and quarters of the year, followed by Ptolemy’s Apotelesmatika, Theophilus’ mundane inceptions, annual astrology, the king’s lot, annual and monthly lords, and Petosiris-Nechepso on auspicious and inauspicious months.
